games.note: Technique sample after Jav's 'The Hall' (X): a derelict service corridor presented as bodycam found footage. 100% procedural Three.js geometry — zero modeled assets — and every texture generated on canvas in code (concrete grime, graffiti, night skyline, the vending-machine face). DOM bodycam overlay: REC, live clock, battery, audio meters, film grain. ~30 s auto-drift loop; drag to look, tap to hold. Peak 71 draw calls, ~3k triangles.
games.title: Bodycam Corridor — Procedural Found Footage

games.note: The bodycam sample grown into a full game: a jump-scare rail horror walk through one condemned building, framed as a single police bodycam investigation (Unit 2210, dispatch on the radio between rooms). The camera walks and looks on its own — the player only STABs, and works one big contextual ACTION button (OPEN / SLAM / HOLD / PUSH / GRAB). 12 rooms stage iconic horror compositions with original procedural figures: hallway twins, the doorway woman, an EXIT-sign hulk charge, a night-vision crawler, the corner, the hatch, a mascot hallway sprint, the door light, the tall one, a wall-eyes chase, a flicker statue, and an empty yellow room. Combat is timing-first: a ~1 s counter window opens every grab, then a pulse strike-window mash (on-pulse thrusts count double, ~20 taps max) — plus two don't-stab decoys with fair tells. All-procedural Three.js + WebAudio, zero external assets. Peak 190 draw calls, ~6.7k triangles.
games.title: Dead Hall — Bodycam Jump-Scare Rail Horror
